newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE SHARE INDEX BREAKS 1,900 SUPPORT.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE SHARE INDEX BREAKS 1,900 SUPPORT.

text.p: The key Straits Times Industrial Index (STII) on Monday afternoon fell through its psychological support at 1,900 points to 1,898.60, down 2.33 percent.
The STII also breached a 31-month low around 1,904 points seen in January 1995.
At 0726 GMT, the STII was at 1,897.64, down by 46.28 ppints or 2.38 percent.
Dealers said the tumble was triggered by a combination of bearish factors, including last Friday's plunge in New York's Dow Jones Industrial Average and weakness in regional stock markets.
Fund managers were also selling due to fears about possible merging of local and foreign tranches in Singapore blue chip stocks.
Singapore's revision over the weekend of 1997 gross domestic product (GDP) growth to between six to seven percent, up from five to seven percent, inspired little confidence.
"This reaction spells some disbelief, because the GDP (forecast) was above what people expected," one broker said.
